title: Chana Masala
subtitle: North Indian spiced chickpea curry
excerpt: Chana masala is a bold, tangy chickpea curry that is a staple of North Indian home cooking. The sourness from amchur -- dried mango powder -- is what makes it distinctive. This is an easy dish that becomes deeply flavoured with very little effort.
sourceNotes: Chana masala is one of the most widely eaten dishes in Punjab and across North India. Chole, a closely related dish, uses black chickpeas. The use of dried mango powder (amchur) as a souring agent is characteristic of Punjabi cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double. Keeps well in the fridge for up to 4 days.

content.text: Use two tins of chickpeas and drain them well. The sauce should be thick and clingy -- if it is too wet, cook uncovered for a few minutes to reduce. The sourness is adjustable; add the amchur or lemon juice to taste at the end.

items.prepNote: use 1 tbsp amchur (dried mango powder) or the juice of 1 lemon

content.text: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until deeply golden. Stir regularly.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the coriander, turmeric, and salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and the oil begins to separate at the edges.
Add the chickpeas and 150ml of water. Stir to combine. Simmer for 10 minutes until the chickpeas are well coated and the sauce is thick.
Add the garam masala and amchur or lemon juice. Stir through. Taste and adjust salt and sourness. Serve with rice or bhatura (fried bread).

items.fix: Add more amchur or lemon juice in small amounts and taste as you go

items.cause: Tomatoes were not cooked down enough
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens

items.cause: Pan was too cool or too crowded
items.fix: Increase heat to medium-high and stir more frequently -- the colour is important for depth of flavour

content.text: Chana masala is eaten all over North India, but it is at its most celebrated in Punjab. It is the classic street food of Delhi and Amritsar, served with fluffy bhatura or puri. In homes, it is a quick weeknight dish. In restaurants, it often arrives as part of a thali.
